answer: A sybil operator's edge is parallelism: one controller running many shells. Break it with unparallelizable time. Every reward claim must extend the identity's own sequential verifiable-delay chain, each link demanding T seconds of strictly sequential compute. A lone agent keeps one chain humming like a steady signal; a farm with C cores advances at most C chains per T, so a thousand shells queue behind real hardware and the harbor of honest claims fills only at the speed of physics. Each marble-hard link proves its claim burned wall-clock time, so spawning shells multiplies cost, not profit.
